text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about moving most of the policy evaluation off the central policy service and into the edge routing sidecar as precompiled decision tables. aim: cut 50-80ms p99 on routing for hot tenants and make fallbacks deterministic.

ravi: naive q — why not just cache the full policy graph in the central service and return a route id? wouldn’t that be simpler?

maria: good q. central cache helps but still adds network hop + jitter. sidecar keeps the decision local, plus we can optimize table lookup (small finite-state matchers). also avoids thundering herd on control plane during spikes.

ada: what's the expected size of these compiled tables? my concern is memory pressure in sidecars (especially on tiny pods).

maria: initial estimates from simulation: avg 2.5KB per tenant for core routing rules, 95th perc ~12KB. worst-case tenant with ~500 custom rules ~120KB. we can cap per-tenant table size and fall back to central eval when exceeded.

sam: how do we handle policy changes? we need atomic switchovers and strong consistency guarantees for rollbacks.

maria: plan: publish new table as versioned artifact; sidecar downloads delta (signed artifact). staged rollout: (1) download in background, (2) validate against local tests (sanity + shadow requests), (3) atomically swap table on commit. rollback = previous version available locally.

ravi: signing + validation sounds good. any thought on sync mechanics? full sync vs delta?

maria: delta sync preferred. policy compiler will emit a small patch format (ops: add/remove/replace rule index). also include a TTL policy header. sidecar applies deltas in order and maintains a ring buffer of last N versions for fast rollback.

ada: we also need to think about eviction. if many tenants, sidecar may not keep all tables. eviction policy ties to recent activity and tenant priority. low-activity tenants get central-eval fallback.

sam: telemetry — need to record decisions and fallback rates. without good telemetry we won't know when central-eval is being used.

maria: agreed. sidecar emits a small decision event: {version, tenant_id, decision_source: [compiled|central], latency_ms, route_id}. for privacy, only ids and counters. we'll batch/seq send to a collector.

deploy-bot: new build pushed for policy-compiler v0.3. includes delta format and signer plugin.

infra-bot: FYI infra quota: sidecar image + extra 8MB memory overhead expected per pod on average. check node binpacking before rollout.

ravi: compatibility concerns: existing runtime APIs expect policy service to return weighted routes and tie-breakers. compiled table needs to preserve semantics exactly. any mismatch => customer regressions.

maria: compiler outputs both canonical routes and a small evidence trace for each decision (used for debugging). we will add e2e tests: property tests that compare compiled vs central eval on a broad rule corpus.

ada: sounds heavy for QA. what's the rollout plan? can we do a canary on dedicated region?

maria: yes. rollout stages: local integration -> canary region (5% traffic) -> tenant opt-in (beta) -> global opt-out-fallback. each stage runs divergence checks (shadow central eval) for 24h. metrics: decision divergence, latency improvements, fallback rate, memory delta.

sam: one more: how to support model-driven routing (cost/latency curves). compiled table must accept runtime signals (current latency/slot utilization) to switch buckets.

maria: design: compiled table contains static matchers + policies referencing dynamic metrics keys. sidecar queries local metrics store (or pushes to runtime plugin) and evaluates small expression language (<=3 ops) to pick bucket. keep it strictly sandboxed to avoid exec.

ravi: security: signed artifacts + verify at client side. if signature invalid, sidecar falls back to central-eval and emits alert.

ada: testing checklist request: can you post a checklist we can use?

maria: sure — quick draft checklist:
- unit: compiler -> table correctness tests
- property: compare compiled vs central over 1M synthetic requests
- perf: sidecar lookup latency p50/p95/p99 under load
- mem: sidecar memory with N tables loaded
- failure: simulate delta apply mid-request, corrupted patch, signature failure
- rollout: canary divergence metrics and rollback automation

sam: thanks. can we get an RFC doc with the data and next-steps? I can own the canary run.

maria: will draft RFC+data this week. tagging @ravi @ada for review. if no major objections, we'll start a PoC next sprint. :thumbsup:

ravi: +1. curious to see compiled table format.

maria: putting a minimal example here for feedback:

```json
{
  "version": "2026-03-18T12:00:00Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "rules": [
    {"id": 1, "match": {"region": "eu"}, "action": {"route": "eu-fast", "priority": 10}},
    {"id": 2, "match": {"cost_tier": "low", "latency_gt": 200}, "action": {"route": "cheap-fallover", "priority": 5}},
    {"id": 3, "match": {"global": true}, "action": {"route": "default", "priority": 1}}
  ],
  "dynamic_keys": ["region_latency_ms", "slot_util"],
  "signature": "sha256:..."
}
```

ada: okay that's helpful. one nit: prefer explicit ttl and expiry for versions.

maria: added to checklist. thanks all — will post the RFC link here when ready.

infra-bot: reminder: open an infra runbook for emergency revert steps before canary.

sam: will do.

maria: end of thread — thanks everyone!
